entities.name: Preterm premature rupture of membranes
observations: At 26 weeks, expectant inpatient management is appropriate only if infection, labor, abruption, and fetal compromise are absent.

entities.name: Intraamniotic infection
observations: Maternal temperature 38.0–38.9°C plus an additional clinical risk factor such as uterine tenderness supports suspected intraamniotic infection.
In PPROM, suspected intraamniotic infection warrants antibiotics and delivery after maternal-fetal stabilization.

entities.name: Fever plus uterine tenderness
observations: A maternal temperature of 38.1°C together with a tender gravid uterus is clinically concerning for intraamniotic infection and is more decisive for delivery than isolated oligohydramnios, leukocytosis, inflammatory-marker elevation, or fetal tachycardia.

entities.name: PMID:25443078
observations: Prospective preliminary study from the Longitudinal Assessment for Bariatric Surgery cohort; 95 participants completed computerized cognitive testing before surgery and at 12 weeks and 12 months postoperatively.
Attention/executive function and memory improved significantly at both 12 weeks and 12 months after bariatric surgery.

Age was not associated with baseline cognitive performance and was not a significant predictor of 12-week or 12-month attention/executive or memory performance after adjustment for baseline performance.
Authors concluded that older age did not preclude postbariatric cognitive benefits, while calling for more age-diverse prospective samples, including adults up to age 70.

entities.name: Age not limiting cognition
observations: In 95 bariatric-surgery participants, older age did not predict poorer postoperative attention/executive or memory performance at 12 weeks or 12 months after controlling for baseline cognition; P>.05 for all age predictors.
